timeline.kind: container (identity edit lists applied by the demuxer)

alignment.method: v2: click gap fingerprint + local onset clock

sync.used_for: coarse identity anchor only; timing comes from the click onsets

reasons: null-control hit fraction 0.25 > 0.05 (detector fires without a click)

quantisation_statement: real-time pts input only (re-timed exports are refused). Each latency is a frame pts minus an audio onset; the light changed within the frame period ending at the detected frame, so every event carries one frame (4.17 ms at 240 fps) of quantisation; its random part averages out over N (about 4.17/sqrt(12 N) ms on the mean) but it biases latency late by 0 to 1 frame
boom_excluded: only truth clicks are scored; BOOM is never paired
limits: Emission versus exposure: the frame pts names a frame, not the instant the LEDs changed; the light changed within the preceding frame period (quantisation, stated per event).

Rolling shutter: each sensor row is read at a different time within the frame; an ROI's rows are exposed later than the frame's pts by its row offset times the readout time. Bound: up to the sensor readout fraction of 1/240 s (at most 4.17 ms; an ROI high in the frame sees less) [INFERENCE, not measured].

iPhone audio/video track offset: any constant offset between the phone's audio and video timelines shifts every latency equally; this tool cannot measure it without an event that is both seen and heard at a known instant [INFERENCE].
Acoustic path: onsets are when the sound reached the phone's microphone, not the Titan's (about 2.9 ms per metre of path difference).
AAC pre-echo can move an audio onset earlier by up to a few milliseconds [INFERENCE].

Responses that darken, or that rise slower than the noise-relative threshold within 300 ms, are MISSES; responses earlier than the onset (negative latency, e.g. from an A/V offset) are not searched (the early-rise count flags them).
Auto-exposure and white balance changes alter luma; lock exposure (AE/AF lock) when recording.

device_alignment.reason: the records carry no audio-derived per-hop field (looked for transient, flux, onset_strength, bass_onset, level, rms), so the SYNC bursts cannot be located in device time. _host_read_s and _music_s are host-clock times (serial read and afplay launch); they include unmeasured host audio-output latency and serial/poll delay, so they are not used to align device stamps to the video. Render and wire-complete stamps are also absent from LiveTimingRecord v2.
